title: Fast-track mini-window ops heatmap + stagger plan (Dec 2026) — draft
content:
Purpose: quick reference and field guide for small-window (<=30m) deploys where we need tight telemetry sampling + staggered backfills. This is a working checklist and heatmap for the Dec 2026 fast-track lanes — keep concise, use for on-call handoffs.

Context / When to use this doc:
- Small non-blocking changes (config flips, minor infra flags, hotfix with minimal schema impact) that must go live inside a 30-minute window.
- Not for large model swaps, migrations, DB schema changes, or multi-region features.
- Prioritizes short SLO-observability loops + deterministic fallback.

Mini-window rollout calendar (UTC) — suggested cadence:
- T-72h: announce deploy window in #deploy-notices and attach quick checklist (owner + pager).
- T-24h: telemetry smoke run (staging traffic replay) — confirm traces and error budgets.
- Day of (UTC):
  - Window A (low-latency critical paths): 02:00 - 02:30 UTC — teams: serving-runtime, sre-core
  - Window B (non-critical infra): 05:00 - 05:30 UTC — teams: platform-engineering, infra
  - Window C (console/observability): 10:00 - 10:30 UTC — teams: console-and-tooling, observability
- Stagger rules: always leave 90m between windows for telemetry maturity and manual rollback if needed.

Ops heatmap (quick view):
- Rows = teams (serving-runtime / platform / sre / console / client-sdk)
- Columns = windows (A/B/C)
- Color hints (ops use): GREEN = go, AMBER = caution (pay attention), RED = block
  - serving-runtime: A=GREEN, B=AMBER, C=AMBER
  - platform-engineering: A=AMBER, B=GREEN, C=AMBER
  - observability: A=AMBER, B=AMBER, C=GREEN
  - sre-core: A=GREEN, B=AMBER, C=AMBER
  - client-sdk: A=AMBER, B=AMBER, C=GREEN

Preflight checklist (T-24h -> T-1h):
- Confirm deploy bundle hash and attach to release notes (owner).
- Run minimal traffic replay to mimic peak 15m QPS for the target microservice. Confirm: 95th latency <= baseline + 10%, error rate < 0.1%
- Validate telemetry ingestion (span + logs) for new code path (observability owner).
- Canary config: set sampling=1.5% unless otherwise specified.
- Rollback stub present in ops dashboard (named release-<hash>-rollback).
- Pager rotation assigned and acknowledged in Slack thread #deploy-ops (include direct pager links).

Day-of deployment steps (owner in parentheses):
1) T-30m: final smoke test in staging (QA / owner).
2) T-15m: snapshot current KV cache metrics, flux metrics, and token throughput (sre). Save snapshot id in linked artifacts.
3) T-5m: flip canary gate for Window A (owner). Announce in #deploy-notices: "Starting Window A — serving-runtime".
4) T+2m: validate traces for first in-flight requests (observability).
5) T+7m: sample end-to-end traces for 10 unique user journeys. If 95th latency spike or error rate > threshold -> trigger rollback (see rollback matrix).
6) T+20m: if amber signals only (minor degradation), pause new traffic and monitor for 15m. If stable, continue to next window after 90m gap.
7) On success, tag release as deployed and update release notes draft (owner).

Rollback matrix (quick):
- Immediate rollback if: sustained error rate > 1% for 3 consecutive minutes OR 95th latency > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Scoped rollback (canary only) if: error spikes in a specific region or instance class — revert canary weights to 0 and route back to previous artifact.
- Emergency full rollback: coordinate with SRE lead and product; declare incident and follow incident comms template.

Post-deploy (T+1h -> T+72h):
- T+1h: post-mortem deck stub prepopulated (owner). Capture metrics, traces, and short summary.
- T+24h: run regression prompts and key evals (if model-adjacent) or smoke tests for APIs.
- T+72h: final signoff from product and SRE; mark release as stable or schedule hotfix.

Release notes — DRAFT (short):
- Title: hotfix/runtime-config-2026-12-xx
- Summary: Small runtime config adjustments to reduce CPU pressure during short bursts; no model changes.
- Impact: rolling deploy across Dedicated and Hosted control planes. Expected user-visible impact: none.
- Rollout plan: mini-window staggered (Windows A/B/C). Full rollback path exists.
- Owner: Maya Patel (release eng) | SRE: Liam O'Neill
- Links: GH PR #4821, JIRA REL-2104

Risk table (short):
- Risk: unexpected latency spike; Mitigation: tight telemetry + 90m stall between windows; Quick action: rollback canary
- Risk: telemetry gap; Mitigation: dedicated sampling and preflight ingestion test
- Risk: cross-region inconsistency; Mitigation: restrict first windows to single region, then expand

Contacts / handoff quick list:
- Release owner: Maya Patel — maya.patel@redwood.com — Slack: @maya
- SRE lead on-call: Liam O'Neill — pager: +1-555-1212 — Slack: @liam
- Observability owner: Sofia Martinez — Slack: @soph

Open questions / TODOs (resolve before T-24h):
- Confirm telemetry retention policy for sampled traces during mini-windows (Sofia).
- Decide canary sample rate default (1.5% vs 2%) for low-volume services (engineering leads).
- Add short checklist for client-sdk consumers if flag toggles are exposed (client-sdk).

Notes / field comments: (freeform)
- This doc is intentionally pithy — use it as a checklist appendix to the main release orchestration page.
- If any window slips more than 15m, escalate to the release coordinator to reschedule downstream windows.
- Keep the release notes short; longer narratives go in the post-mortem deck.

Revision log:
- 2026-12-20 — initial draft (Maya Patel)
- 2026-12-22 — added stagger rule and heatmap color hints (Liam O'Neill)

(End of draft)
